markdown_report:
Prioritize a bounded catalog-ranking audit after the existing BERT4Rec integrity checks. At 20% progress, this offers an actionable next experiment without changing the trained model. Strengthen it with exact sampled-hit expectations, explicit eligibility policies, and numerical checks; repeated sampling becomes calibration rather than the primary estimator.

Three insights follow from the starting point. First, consumed-batch provenance establishes alignment only on captured examples. It cannot establish catalog-ranking quality. Second, Electronics’ negative-outranks-positive rate varies from 10.25% to 21.97% across supplied attempts. These training-exposed observations identify neither a cause nor a validation winner. Third, exported-predictor parity remains uncertified. Catalog diagnostics must identify their scoring path and retain that limitation.

Three insights follow from related work. BERT4Rec uses bidirectional reconstruction [1]. Next-item diagnostics require strictly earlier context and an appended mask. Sampled metrics can reverse aggregate model comparisons even in expectation [2]. More candidate draws estimate the sampled quantity more precisely, rather than recovering catalog HR@10. Frequency-group tradeoffs [3] and repetition differences [7] motivate stratification. Neither establishes a shortcut in these checkpoints.

These insights organize three directions: supervision integrity, candidate-set robustness, and deployment consistency. Their conceptual map is:

| Direction | Evidence unit | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Existing provenance replay | Consumed event and loss | Catalog competition |
| Proposed rank audit | Fixed prefix, eligibility, and candidate universe | Held-out generalization |
| Predictor parity | Reloaded item-associated scores | User usefulness |

Three atomic ideas merit consideration. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means more implementation effort.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Catalog versus sampled rank audit [1–7] | 4/7/5 | Exact sampling baseline; reusable; no retraining | Established components; no direct accuracy gain; numerical integration |
| Frequency-matched negative stress test [2,3] | 3/6/3 | Interpretable frequency control; simple reuse | Bin choices and sparse bins matter; relevance remains unknown |
| Exported-predictor score parity | 2/8/4 | Resolves deployment uncertainty; broadly useful; no retraining | Engineering contribution; no usefulness guarantee; runner integration |

Select the first idea. Freeze one checkpoint/category and select at most 50 training users/category with seed 42 and at least two events. Use each user's last training target, complete preceding history H, and retained window W of at most L−1 events. Preserve earlier repeats, append MASK, left-pad, and read its final absolute position.

Declare primary eligibility C_H=(I\H)∪{target}; additionally report C_W=(I\W)∪{target}. These target-restored policies differ from strict unseen-item evaluation, which excludes repeated targets. Report unseen targets, repeats within W, and repeats only outside W separately. With identical scores, rank under C_H cannot exceed rank under C_W; this is a filtering consequence.

Score fixed catalog chunks twice: obtain the target score from its own chunk, then count eligible predecessors using descending score and ascending item ID. Exclude the target explicitly. Disable autocast, use FP32 operands and IEEE FP32 matmul controls, and reject nonfinite scores before filtering [4,5]. Chunking need not reproduce unchunked ranks near ties. Check bounded fixtures across chunk sizes, irregular tails, duplicate embeddings, near ties, exclusions, and target boundaries; record rank discrepancies, precision settings, and software/hardware [4–6].

If N eligible negatives contain K predecessors, catalog rank is K+1. For m=min(99,N) unique uniform negatives, X follows Hypergeometric(N,K,m), giving expected sampled HR@10=P(X≤9). Compute its CDF stably. Average user probabilities; retain seeds 42/43/44 as optional, separately reported calibration draws. Every catalog hit must remain a sampled hit. Disagreement otherwise measures candidate sensitivity, not implementation failure or model superiority.

Report ranks, expected and realized sampled hits, sampled-hit/catalog-miss rates, counts, and popularity/history strata. Bootstrap users within category, retaining draws together; macro-average only with all four categories represented. Preserve interfaces, routing, seeds, ceilings, trial-local artifacts, and one model/category. Log shared-budget diagnostic cost and unavailable checks. Only unchanged host macro validation HR@10 selects revisions; training recovery does not establish generalization or immediate usefulness.

idea.description: Add a bounded streaming catalog-ranking diagnostic to corrected single-model BERT4Rec, comparing training-prefix catalog ranks with exact uniform-without-replacement sampled-hit expectations and optional reproducible calibration draws under explicit history-filtering policies.
idea.motivation: Existing training margins do not establish catalog competition, deployed-predictor consistency, or validation gains. Exact hypergeometric expectations distinguish predictable candidate-set effects from implementation inconsistencies, while explicit full-history and retained-window eligibility separates filtering effects from modeling effects.
idea.implementation_notes:
This remains an integration specification because the baseline source is absent. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and every ModelView interface. view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module; preserve item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data. Preserve diagnostic tuples (None, sequence, positive, negative) with B×L tensors. Gate the audit on applicable structural checks and report unresolved provenance and fresh-process predictor parity independently. Exercise the existing family-specific scoring path; do not claim that live scoring certifies the embedded predictor.

Predeclare at most 50 eligible training users/category, selected without replacement using a dedicated seed-42 RNG. Sort category and user identifiers using a recorded canonical ordering before selection. Eligible users have at least two training events and valid catalog IDs. Choose each user's final training event as target, retaining its event identity. Let H contain every strictly preceding event and W=H[-(L-1):], with L>=2. Preserve earlier occurrences of the target item. Construct left_pad(W+[MASK], L) and read the appended mask's absolute position, which is L-1 for this construction. Never use nonpadding-count minus one. Do not access validation or test events for diagnostic construction.

Let I be the fixed mapped real-item catalog, excluding padding and MASK. Primary target-restored eligibility is C_H=(I minus set(H)) union {target}; secondary eligibility is C_W=(I minus set(W)) union {target}. Include the target exactly once. Report both policies on the same selected users and scores. Classify users into target unseen in H, target repeated within W, and target repeated only outside W. Report counts and metrics per category and stratum. Strict unseen-item summaries include only targets absent from H and explicitly report excluded repeated targets; do not silently replace excluded users. These diagnostic policies do not change the native full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for the twenty designated users, five/category. Rank_H<=rank_W follows from C_H being a subset of C_W under identical scores and ties; it is not a modeling improvement.

Run in evaluation/inference mode, restoring every module's prior mode and main-process Python, NumPy, CPU Torch, and CUDA RNG states in finally. Do not advance the production loader. Restore any modified global precision controls as well. Main-process restoration does not restore worker-local state. Freeze checkpoint parameters and compute one appended-mask representation per prefix. Record encoder dtype separately from scorer dtype: casting already-rounded features or embeddings cannot recover earlier precision loss.

Define the catalog score computation using a fixed item-ID order, chunk size, final-chunk policy, scorer, device, and precision configuration. Disable autocast around scoring, cast both scorer operands to FP32, and select IEEE FP32 matrix multiplication with controls supported by the installed PyTorch version; record the effective settings and TF32 status. Do not silently substitute a different scoring function for predict_score. If the existing scorer cannot honor these settings, report the limitation. In a first pass, score every catalog chunk, reject any unexpected NaN/Inf before eligibility masking, and extract the target's score from its own catalog chunk. In a second pass, replay identical chunks, shapes, and settings and count eligible competitors preceding that fixed target score. Explicitly exclude the target. Require repeated target scoring to agree under the recorded deterministic configuration; investigate disagreement rather than quietly changing tolerances. Use descending score, then ascending mapped item ID, with exact equality for ties and no epsilon ties. This defines an exhaustive rank under the declared chunked computation, not bitwise equivalence to every possible unchunked computation.

For sampled calibration, reuse scores generated by that same catalog computation. Retain only each draw's selected scores while streaming, rather than rescoring narrow candidate matrices whose numerical behavior may differ. For each eligibility policy, let N=|C|-1 and K=rank-1. Set m=min(99,N). Uniformly selecting m distinct eligible negatives gives X~Hypergeometric(N,K,m), sampled rank X+1, and expected sampled HR@10=P(X<=9). Compute the CDF using scipy.stats.hypergeom.cdf with population N, successes K, and draws m; handle N=0 explicitly as probability one. Record support bounds, N, K, m, and finite probabilities in [0,1]. The expected sampled-hit/catalog-miss rate per user is 1{K>9}P(X<=9). Every catalog hit must remain a sampled hit; validate this implication with identical scores, eligibility, and tie rules. The formula applies only to uniform sampling without replacement. Do not apply it to nonuniform or duplicate-containing candidate generation, and do not assume that host sampling has this exact eligibility policy.

Exact expectations replace repeated draws as the primary sampled-metric estimator. Retain diagnostic seeds 42, 43, and 44 as optional calibration draws, each using its own dedicated RNG and a fixed category/user traversal. Include the positive exactly once and sample m unique eligible negatives. Report actual candidate counts, sampled ranks, each draw's HR@10, rank variability, and hit flips separately. Small candidate universes with at most nine negatives necessarily yield HR@10=1 and must remain visible. Three draws cannot establish detailed calibration; any formal statistical discrepancy test requires a separately predeclared statistic, sufficient simulation, and multiplicity handling. A surviving catalog miss in a sample is expected, not an implementation failure. Never tune the scorer or eligibility to make observed draws resemble a desired outcome.

Predeclare bounded correctness fixtures: empty and short contexts, full-length retained windows, unequal left padding, repeated items, duplicate embeddings, near ties, target at chunk boundaries, irregular final chunks, exclusions, empty negative universes, and injected NaN/Inf. On small fixtures, compare streaming scores, exact ranks, and top-k with unchunked FP32 scoring across fixed chunk sizes. Establish item-ID order before any stable score sort; ordinary topk does not guarantee stable ties. Check exact rank/top-k agreement separately from score tolerance, using rtol=1.3e-6 and atol=1e-5 as recorded initial score-comparison tolerances. Record near-tie rank changes even when scores pass tolerance. Require agreement on fixtures with adequate score separation; investigate discrepancies and retain the fixed production chunk policy rather than asserting universal numerical invariance. Validate the hypergeometric calculation against exhaustive subset enumeration on small N and test rank_H<=rank_W and catalog-hit-implies-sampled-hit. These checks require no retraining.

Report training-exposed catalog HR@10, exact expected sampled HR@10, their paired difference, expected sampled-hit/catalog-miss rate, catalog-rank summaries, and optional realized sampled results. Record denominators and actual candidate sizes. Stratify by repeat status, retained-prefix length, and target training frequency. Compute frequency from supplied training interactions only; use recorded catalog-frequency quartile cutpoints and selected-prefix-length quartile cutpoints, with an explicit boundary convention such as numpy.searchsorted(cutpoints, value, side='right'). Report tied cutpoints and empty strata. For 1,000 seed-42 bootstrap replicates, resample users within each category, keeping each user's policies, strata, and candidate draws together; calculate percentile 95% intervals for paired diagnostic differences. Report each calibration draw separately. Compute equal-category macro summaries only when all four categories have valid observations; otherwise return null with a reason. Intervals condition on selected users, candidate policy, and fitted checkpoints, excluding training-seed and adaptive-selection uncertainty. Exact sampling expectations remove candidate Monte Carlo error from the primary estimate but not cohort uncertainty.

Bound and log diagnostic GPU time, completed users, catalog chunks, failures, and interruptions against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Return unavailable reasons instead of healthy zeros; do not fabricate completed summaries. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, single-GPU execution, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per completed epoch, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four category routes, and trial-local artifacts. Preserve the existing checkpoint configuration and embedded predictor writer; any later inference change must update both. Deploy exactly one independently trained checkpoint/category without averaging, score fusion, additional fitted scorers, or reuse of other trials. No additional datasets or pretrained weights are introduced. Preserve existing family-safe integrity, margin, and embedding probes. Ratings, review text, commercial attributes, item-category metadata, and simulator traits remain unavailable rather than inferred. Qualitative feedback supplies hypotheses, not observed compatibility, ownership, mood, or purchase labels.

The audit adds no learned component, so it introduces no new training shortcut itself. Existing memorization, frequency shortcuts, and repeated-target advantages can remain despite passing checks. Repeated diagnostic inspection and adaptive model selection can overfit the fixed validation cohort; log diagnostic and validation queries and predeclare follow-up experiments. Retain the frequency-matched stress test as a later separate composition intervention and exported-predictor parity as an independent deployment audit. Only the unchanged pinned host macro validation HR@10 selects revisions; catalog training recovery and analytic sampled expectations never replace it.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        state = save_module_modes_main_process_rng_and_precision_controls()
        try:
            view.model.eval()
            with inference_mode():
                result = existing_family_safe_diagnostics_without_advancing_production_loader()
                if required_structural_checks_failed(result):
                    return add_unavailable_catalog_audit(result, 'structural failure')
                run_bounded_rank_precision_eligibility_and_hypergeometric_fixtures()
                configure_supported_ieee_fp32_scoring_and_disable_autocast()
                users = seeded_select_from_canonical_training_users(limit=50, seed=42)
                for user in users:
                    H, target = complete_training_history(user)[:-1], complete_training_history(user)[-1]
                    W = H[-(L - 1):]
                    tokens = left_pad(W + [MASK], L)
                    features = view.log2feats(tokens)[:, L - 1]
                    policies = {
                        'full_history_target_restored': (I - set(H)) | {target},
                        'window_target_restored': (I - set(W)) | {target}
                    }
                    draws = optional_unique_uniform_draws(policies, target, seeds=[42, 43, 44])
                    target_score = None
                    for chunk in fixed_catalog_chunks(I):
                        scores = score_via_existing_scorer_fp32(features, chunk)
                        require_all_finite_before_filtering(scores)
                        if target in chunk:
                            target_score = score_associated_with_id(scores, chunk, target)
                    K = {policy: 0 for policy in policies}
                    draw_scores = initialize_bounded_draw_score_storage(draws)
                    for chunk in identical_catalog_chunks(I):
                        scores = score_via_existing_scorer_fp32(features, chunk)
                        require_all_finite_before_filtering(scores)
                        verify_repeated_target_score_if_present(chunk, scores, target_score)
                        for policy, eligible in policies.items():
                            K[policy] += count_eligible_ids_other_than_target(
                                chunk, scores, eligible, target,
                                condition='score > target_score OR (score == target_score AND id < target)')
                        retain_selected_draw_scores_from_this_same_catalog_pass(draw_scores, chunk, scores)
                    require(K['full_history_target_restored'] <= K['window_target_restored'])
                    for policy, eligible in policies.items():
                        N = len(eligible) - 1
                        m = min(99, N)
                        expected_hit = 1.0 if N == 0 else hypergeom.cdf(9, N, K[policy], m)
                        catalog_hit = int(K[policy] <= 9)
                        expected_sampled_hit_catalog_miss = (1 - catalog_hit) * expected_hit
                        record_counts_ranks_expectations_and_repeat_stratum(
                            user, policy, N, m, K[policy] + 1, expected_hit,
                            expected_sampled_hit_catalog_miss, H, W, target)
                        for draw in optional_draws_for_policy(draws, policy):
                            sampled_rank = rank_from_retained_catalog_scores(
                                target, target_score, draw_scores[draw], tie_rule='ascending_item_id')
                            require(not catalog_hit or sampled_rank <= 10)
                            record_draw_separately(draw, sampled_rank, candidate_count=m + 1)
                aggregate_categories_strata_and_1000_paired_user_bootstraps(seed=42)
                macro_average_only_if_all_four_categories_have_valid_observations()
                record_cost_completion_counts_precision_and_unavailable_checks()
                return {'metrics': result.metrics, 'metric_definitions': result.definitions}
        finally:
            restore_module_modes_main_process_rng_and_precision_controls(state)

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return interpretation_prompt(
        raw_diagnosis,
        require=['measured metrics', 'definitions', 'denominators', 'eligibility policies',
                 'repeat strata', 'analytic sampling assumptions', 'precision settings',
                 'rank discrepancies', 'unavailable reasons', 'diagnostic cost'],
        distinguish=['training recovery', 'expected sampled metric', 'catalog metric',
                     'filtering effects', 'predictor parity', 'host validation'],
        prohibit=['invented gains', 'causal preference claims', 'ensemble proposals',
                  'treating expected sampled/catalog disagreement as a bug'])

originality.positive: Combines event-aligned BERT4Rec recovery, explicit eligibility contrasts, exhaustive ranks, and an exact sampling baseline within the existing diagnostic contract.
originality.negative: Hypergeometric sampling, streaming ranks, and numerical checks are established methods; their integration does not introduce a new learning principle.

future_potential.positive: Separates candidate-size, filtering, repetition, and numerical effects, producing clearer evidence for subsequent controlled single-model experiments.
future_potential.negative: Training recovery remains exposure-confounded; stronger audit validity does not itself improve validation HR@10 or demonstrate immediate usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses one encoder and scorer, needs no retraining, and replaces primary Monte Carlo estimation with a standard hypergeometric CDF.
code_difficulty.negative: Two-pass score consistency, version-dependent precision controls, scorer-shape behavior, eligibility strata, calibration, and uncertainty reporting exceed a simple chunked-ranking implementation.

related_work.title: [1] BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Provides the family-specific basis for appended-mask next-item scoring.
limitations: Interior reconstruction and terminal prediction have different available context.
The objective does not certify this implementation's integrity, deployed-predictor parity, or ranking quality.

related_work.title: [2] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can produce inconsistent aggregate model comparisons, including in expectation.
Motivates distinguishing sampled expectations from full-catalog metrics; uniform sampling without replacement admits the stated hypergeometric specialization.
limitations: Does not establish a specific failure in the supplied checkpoints.
Does not justify changing the pinned host validation protocol.
The hypergeometric specialization requires fixed scores, eligibility, ordering, and uniform distinct-negative sampling.

related_work.title: [3] Sequential recommendation negative-sampling study supplied in the search results
contributions: The supplied summary reports head, middle, and tail accuracy differences under alternative negative-sampling policies.
Motivates training-frequency stratification and a separately specified frequency-matched stress test.
limitations: Reported tradeoffs do not establish a popularity shortcut in these checkpoints.
Frequency matching changes candidate composition and is not an unbiased relevance estimator.
The uniform hypergeometric baseline cannot automatically be applied to nonuniform candidate generation.

related_work.title: [4] PyTorch Numerical Accuracy
contributions: Documents floating-point differences between mathematically equivalent whole-tensor and sliced computations.
Supports checking score and rank behavior across chunk shapes and precision settings.
limitations: Obtaining the target score from its catalog chunk and replaying identical chunks is an implementation protocol motivated by the guidance.

related_work.title: [5] PyTorch CUDA Semantics and Precision Controls
contributions: Documents controls affecting CUDA matrix multiplication precision, including TF32 behavior.
Supports explicitly recording effective precision rather than inferring arithmetic precision from output dtype.
limitations: Available controls depend on the installed PyTorch version and hardware.
FP32 casting cannot recover information already lost in earlier lower-precision computation.

related_work.title: [6] PyTorch Reproducibility
contributions: Documents reproducibility controls and their practical limits.
Motivates recording RNG handling, hardware, software, and deterministic settings.
limitations: Deterministic settings do not guarantee identical results across platforms, versions, or computation shapes.
Restoring main-process RNG states does not restore production-loader progress or worker-local state.

related_work.title: [7] Li et al. (2023), repetition and exploration study supplied in the search results
contributions: Motivates separating repetition and exploration behavior rather than relying solely on aggregate accuracy.
Supports explicit reporting of repeated and previously unseen targets.
limitations: Does not establish the magnitude or cause of repetition effects in these four datasets.
The within-window versus outside-window strata are proposed operational controls for this audit.

related_work.title: PyTorch torch.sort
contributions: Documents stable sorting, which preserves a previously established item-ID order among equal scores.
Supports deterministic score-and-item-ID ordering in bounded rank and top-k fixtures.
limitations: Stable sorting does not remove numerical score differences across computation shapes.
Full-catalog sorting is unnecessary when only a target's rank is required.
